post.description: This week's or next week's projected points and stat lines for a football position, rest-of-season projections, or NBA fantasy basketball season and scoring-period projections.

limit.description:
Return only the top N rows. Omit for the whole table.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 200.

position.description:
Football: QB, RB, WR, TE, K or DST (team defense and special teams). Basketball: PG, SG, SF, PF, C, or G (guards) and F (forwards).

Provider reference: allowed values ["QB", "RB", "WR", "TE", "K", "DST", "PG", "SG", "SF", "PF", "C", "G", "F"].

scoring.description:
Football only: PPR (a point per reception, the default) or STD (non-PPR). The site publishes no half-PPR tables. Omit for basketball, whose tables use CBS points scoring.

Provider reference: allowed values ["PPR", "STD"].

sport.description:
football (default, NFL) or basketball (NBA). Positions, scoring and periods differ by sport; an option of the other sport is invalid_input.

Provider reference: allowed values ["football", "basketball"]; default "football".

type.description:
weekly or ros (rest of season). Defaults to weekly for football and ros for basketball.

Provider reference: allowed values ["weekly", "ros"].

week.description:
Weekly type only. Football: NFL week 1-18; omit for the current week. The site publishes the current and the next week; any other week is not_found. Basketball: a scoring period; the site publishes the next two; omit for the rest of the current period.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 30.

200.description:
CBS Sports fantasy projections for one position: projected fantasy points and the projected stat line for the top 100 players. Football (GET www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/stats/{position}/{season}/{period}/projections/{ppr|nonppr}/): weekly projections exist for the current and the next week; ros is the rest of the season. Basketball (GET www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/stats/{position}/{season}/{period}/projections/): ros (default) is the rest of the season, which before the season starts is the full-season projection (projection_type season); weekly with week is one of the next two scoring periods, and weekly without week is the rest of the current scoring period.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `players` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fantasy_points` | number | Fantasy points in the requested scoring; null where the site shows a dash (did not play), and always null for basketball, whose tables give points per game only. |
| `fantasy_points_per_game` | number | Fantasy points per game. For basketball this is the site's fpts column, which is a per-game average. |
| `name` | string | Player name, or the team's city for football DST. |
| `player_id` | number | CBS Sports player id; null for football team defenses. |
| `player_url` | string | The player's fantasy page, or the team page for football DST. |
| `position` | string |  |
| `stats` | object | The stat line keyed by the site's column codes; the set depends on the sport and position. Football: gp, passing_yds, rushing_td, receiving_rec, fg_fgm, xp_xpm, sck, yards_allowed_total, ... Basketball: gp, gs, min, mpg, fgm, fga, fg_pct, ftm, fta, ft_pct, 3pm, 3pa, 3fg_pct, pts, ppg, reb, rpg, ast, apg, stl, spg, to, topg, blk, bpg (percentages as the site shows them, 0-100). Null where the site shows a dash. |
| `team` | string | Team abbreviation as the site writes it (JAC, WAS, GS, NY). |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

limit.description:
Return only the top N rows. Omit for the whole table.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 200.

position.description:
Football: QB, RB, WR, TE, K, DST, FLX (top 150 RB/WR/TE, weekly only) or ALL (top 200, draft only). Basketball: G (guards), F (forwards), C (centers) or ALL (top 200).

Provider reference: allowed values ["QB", "RB", "WR", "TE", "K", "DST", "FLX", "ALL", "G", "F", "C"].

scoring.description:
Football only: PPR (a point per reception, the default) or STD (non-PPR). The site publishes no half-PPR tables. Omit for basketball, whose rankings are roto.

Provider reference: allowed values ["PPR", "STD"].

sport.description:
football (default, NFL) or basketball (NBA). Positions, scoring and periods differ by sport; an option of the other sport is invalid_input.

Provider reference: allowed values ["football", "basketball"]; default "football".

type.description:
Football only: weekly (default), the current week, or draft, the preseason draft rankings. Omit for basketball, which publishes one list.

Provider reference: allowed values ["weekly", "draft"].

200.description:
CBS Sports fantasy rankings. Football (GET www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/rankings/{ppr|standard}/{list}/{weekly|yearly}/): the consensus rank of each player with every expert's own rank, opponent (weekly) or bye week and auction value (draft); FLX is the weekly top 150 RB/WR/TE and ALL the draft top 200. Basketball (GET www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/rankings/roto/{G|F|C|top200}/): RotoWire's rankings for a 12-team, 8-category roto league, as rank and player only; ALL is the top 200 with each player's position.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `players` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auction_value` | number | Football draft only: suggested salary-cap auction value in dollars; null otherwise. |
| `bye_week` | number | Football draft only; null otherwise. |
| `expert_ranks` | object[] | Each expert's rank, in the experts order; empty for basketball. |
| `name` | string | Player name, or the team nickname for football DST. |
| `opponent` | string | Football weekly only: "vs. NYJ" / "at NYJ"; null for draft and basketball. |
| `player_id` | number | CBS Sports player id; null for football team defenses. |
| `player_url` | string | The player's fantasy page; null for football DST. |
| `pos_rank` | string | Positional rank label, for example RB1 or G1; null on the basketball ALL list, which gives no positional rank. |
| `position` | string | Position; for basketball the list position (G, F, C), or the player's position on the ALL list. |
| `rank_ecr` | number | The site's consensus rank in the list. |
| `team` | string | Team abbreviation as the site writes it (JAC, WAS); null for basketball, whose rankings name no team. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

period.description:
Basketball only, current season, without week: yesterday, the last 7/14/21/28 days, or the three-year averages (published before the season starts). Periods the site is not showing are not_found.

Provider reference: allowed values ["yesterday", "last_7_days", "last_14_days", "last_21_days", "last_28_days", "three_year_average"].

scoring.description:
Football only: PPR (a point per reception, the default) or STD (non-PPR). The site publishes no half-PPR tables. Omit for basketball, whose tables use CBS points scoring.

Provider reference: allowed values ["PPR", "STD"].

season.description:
Season year; an NBA season is labelled by the year it starts (2025 is 2025-26). Omit for the current season. The site publishes the current and the two previous seasons (three before an NBA season starts); others are not_found.

Provider reference: minimum 2000; maximum 2100.

sport.description:
football (default, NFL) or basketball (NBA). Positions, scoring and periods differ by sport; an option of the other sport is invalid_input.

Provider reference: allowed values ["football", "basketball"]; default "football".

week.description:
Current season only; omit for season totals. Football: a single NFL week 1-18; the site publishes only the last completed week. Basketball: a scoring period; the site publishes only the current one ("This Period"). Others are not_found.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 30.
